# Keyboard operability and focus indicator remediation for core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard accessibility defects identified by the accessibility
audit in the four audited core Dashboard flows: project creation, workbench spawn,
model deployment, and pipeline run submission. Today these flows cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable, and
focus indicators are inconsistent. This epic makes all four flows fully operable by
keyboard with consistent, visible focus indicators, restoring the conformance level
that the updated accessibility documentation will subsequently assert.

## Scope

- Remediate every defect the accessibility audit enumerates for the four audited
  flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run
  submission) in the Dashboard.
- Eliminate focus traps and focus loss when modals open and close within the audited
  flows, returning focus to the control that invoked the modal on close.
- Make every control in the audited flows reachable and operable by keyboard alone.
- Make visible focus indicators consistent across all interactive controls in the
  audited flows.
- Out of scope (per strategy): screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes
  require, and any flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given any of the four audited core flows, when a user completes the flow using
  keyboard input alone, then the flow can be completed end to end with no focus traps
  and no unreachable controls — measured by completing each of the four flows with
  keyboard only.
- Given a modal in any of the audited flows, when it opens and later closes, then
  focus moves into the modal on open and returns to the control that invoked it on
  close.
- Given the interactive controls of the audited flows, when an element receives
  keyboard focus, then a visible focus indicator is displayed with a consistent style
  across all four flows — measured by reviewing the focus states of the audited
  controls.
- Given the audit report's enumerated defects, when remediation is complete, then
  every enumerated defect in the four audited flows is fixed or explicitly
  dispositioned with rationale.
- Given the remediated flows, when exercised with pointer input, then prior
  non-keyboard behavior is unchanged (no functional regression), and the Dashboard's
  existing build and test pipeline remains green.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): the four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no
  focus traps or unreachable controls — covered by this epic.
- HLR-2 (P1): visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows —
  covered by this epic.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation to
reflect the fixed state of the four audited Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission): the VPAT conformance
statement and the product documentation accessibility statement. Two public-sector
customers require an updated, published conformance statement before renewal, so the
published documentation is a first-class deliverable of the strategy, not an
incidental follow-up. The documentation must technically match the implemented
keyboard accessibility state of the audited flows.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT (conformance statement) to reflect the conformance state of the
  four audited core flows after the Dashboard keyboard accessibility fixes are
  complete.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to reflect the fixed
  state.
- Republish both documents at their existing public documentation location.
- Obtain technical review of the updated documents against the implemented behavior
  before publication.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the completed keyboard accessibility fixes in the Dashboard, when the VPAT is
  updated, then every documented conformance claim maps to the implemented behavior
  of the four audited flows — measured by tracing each claim to the fixed behavior.
- Given the product documentation, when the accessibility statement is updated and
  republished, then it reflects the current conformance posture and is live at the
  existing public documentation location.
- The updated VPAT and accessibility statement are technically reviewed against the
  implementation, and the review confirms the documented claims match the shipped
  behavior.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P2): the accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs
  accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state,
  with technical review — covered by this epic.
